# bevy_mod_indigauge - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bevy-mod-indigauge/0.6.7/bevy_mod_indigauge/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#indigauge-game-sdk-bevy)Indigauge Game SDK (Bevy)

The **Indigauge Game SDK** is a lightweight Rust library for sending structured analytics and player feedback from your **Bevy** games to the [Indigauge](https://www.indigauge.com) API.

It’s designed to be easy to integrate and is powerful enough for production use in indie games.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- **Bevy 0.18 compatible**— easy drop-in plugin
- Lightweight event macros: `ig_info!`,`ig_warn!`,`ig_error!`, …
- Built-in **Feedback UI panel**for in-game bug reports & suggestions
- Works on both **native**and**WASM**builds*
- **Tracing support**— log events to the Indigauge API through tracing

[!WARNING] On wasm builds, the panic handler is disabled. No crash reports will be sent as events to the Indigauge API.

[§](https://docs.rs#installation)Installation

```
[dependencies]
bevy = "0.18"
bevy-mod-indigauge = { version = "0.6" }
```
[§](https://docs.rs#feedback-backend-features)Feedback backend features

- `feedback`(default): feedback panel rendered with Bevy UI + picking
- `feedback_egui`(optional): render feedback panel with- `bevy_egui`

```
# Keep default Bevy UI panel (no extra feature needed)
bevy-mod-indigauge = { version = "0.6" }
# Enable optional bevy_egui feedback panel backend (native only)
bevy-mod-indigauge = { version = "0.6", features = ["feedback_egui"] }
```
[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

- `minimal`
- `breakout`
- `feedback_egui`- `bevy_egui`feedback panel triggers and props.

[§](https://docs.rs#running-examples)Running Examples

`cargo run --release --example minimal````
cargo run --release --example breakout
# Or with tracing feature:
cargo run --release --example breakout --features tracing
# Run the bevy_egui feedback demo (optional feature)
cargo run --release --example feedback_egui --features feedback_egui
```
[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start)Quick Start

- Setup game project [Indigauge](https://www.indigauge.com)
- Create a public key for the game.
- Add the plugin to your game.

```
use std::time::Duration;
use bevy::{prelude::*, time::common_conditions::on_timer};
use bevy_mod_indigauge::prelude::*;
fn main() {
  App::new()
    .add_plugins(DefaultPlugins)
    .add_plugins(
      IndigaugePlugin::<EmptySessionMeta>::new(
        "YOUR_PUBLIC_KEY",
        "My game name",
        env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")
      )
      // Optional: Set mode (Defaults to live). Dev mode is useful for testing and debugging and does not send events to the server.
      .mode(IndigaugeMode::Dev)
      // Optional: Set preferred log-level (Defaults to Info)
      .log_level(IndigaugeLogLevel::Info)
    )
    .add_systems(Startup, setup)
    .add_systems(Update, (trigger_feedback_with_question, track_counter.run_if(on_timer(Duration::from_secs(2)))))
    .run();
}
fn setup(mut commands: Commands) {
  commands.spawn((Camera2d, IsDefaultUiCamera));
  commands.trigger(StartSessionEvent::new());
}
fn trigger_feedback_with_question(
  mut commands: Commands,
  keys: Res<ButtonInput<KeyCode>>,
) {
  if keys.just_pressed(KeyCode::KeyF) {
    // This is how you manually trigger the feedback panel
    commands.insert_resource(
      FeedbackPanelProps::with_question("What did you think about level 3?", FeedbackCategory::Gameplay),
    );
  }
}
fn track_counter(mut counter: Local<u32>) {
  *counter += 1;
  ig_info!("counter.increase", { "value": *counter });
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#sending-events)Sending events

Send structured events with macros. The events will only be sent if a session was successfully started.

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
ig_info!("player.jump", { "height": 2.4 });
ig_error!("physics.failed", { "component": "rigid_body" });
```
[§](https://docs.rs#tracing-support)Tracing support

Send events to the Indigauge API through tracing. This is useful for debugging and monitoring your game.

[§](https://docs.rs#enable-the-tracing-feature)Enable the tracing feature

```
[dependencies]
bevy = { version = "0.18" }
bevy-mod-indigauge = { version = "0.6", features = ["tracing"] }
```
[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use std::time::Duration;
use bevy::{log::{LogPlugin, BoxedLayer}, prelude::*, time::common_conditions::on_timer};
use bevy_mod_indigauge::{prelude::*, tracing::{IndigaugeLayer, default_bevy_indigauge_layer}};
/// Default tracing layer, will send all events to the Indigauge API.
pub fn default_indigauge_layer(_app: &mut App) -> Option<BoxedLayer> {
  Some(Box::new(default_bevy_indigauge_layer()))
}
/// Custom tracing layer, will only send events that has an event_type, is either info, warn, or
/// error and is not from the bevy_mod_othercrate module to the Indigauge API.
pub fn custom_indigauge_layer(_app: &mut App) -> Option<BoxedLayer> {
  Some(Box::new(
    default_bevy_indigauge_layer()
      .with_event_type_required(true)
      .with_filters(vec!["bevy_mod_othercrate"])
      .with_levels(vec![
        IndigaugeLogLevel::Info,
        IndigaugeLogLevel::Warn,
        IndigaugeLogLevel::Error,
      ]),
  ))
}
fn main() {
  App::new()
    .add_plugins(DefaultPlugins.set(LogPlugin {custom_layer: custom_indigauge_layer, ..default()}))
    .add_plugins(IndigaugePlugin::<EmptySessionMeta>::new("YOUR_PUBLIC_KEY", "My game name", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")))
    .add_systems(Startup, setup)
    .add_systems(Update, (track_counter.run_if(on_timer(Duration::from_secs(2)))))
    .run();
}
fn setup(mut commands: Commands) {
  commands.spawn((Camera2d, IsDefaultUiCamera));
  commands.trigger(StartSessionEvent::new());
}
fn track_counter(mut counter: Local<u32>) {
  *counter += 1;
  info!(ig = "counter.increase", value = *counter);
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#bevy-compatibility)Bevy Compatibility

| bevy | bevy-mod-indigauge |
|---|---|
| 0.18 | 0.6 |
| 0.17 | 0.5 |
| 0.16 | 0.4 |
| 0.15 | 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 |

# gdscript-scene 0.5.4 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/gdscript-scene/0.5.4

# gdscript-scene

A ** .tscn/.tres parser** that feeds node-path typing — so

`$Node`,
`%Unique`, and `get_node(...)` are typed against the actual scene tree. This is
the scene-aware capability the engine's own LSP doesn't fully provide.An internal layer of ** gdscript-analyzer**,
a fast, embeddable GDScript (Godot 4.x) static-analysis library ("Roslyn for
Godot"). You normally don't depend on this crate directly — use

**(the public API), or the**

`gdscript-ide`**(Node) /**

`@gdscript-analyzer/core`**(browser) packages.**

`@gdscript-analyzer/wasm`- **API docs:**- [https://docs.rs/gdscript-scene](https://docs.rs/gdscript-scene)
- **Crate map:**- [repo README](https://github.com/yanivkalfa/gdscript-analyzer#the-workspace--crates--packages)
- **License:**MIT OR Apache-2.0

---

# gdscript_base - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gdscript-base/^0.5.2/

## Expand description

`gdscript-base` — foundational POD types shared across the gdscript-analyzer.

The lowest layer of the crate stack (`plans/01-ARCHITECTURE.md` §1). It holds the
engine-/protocol-neutral, `serde`-serializable result structs every client maps to
its own protocol, plus byte-offset position types and a [ LineIndex](https://docs.rs/struct.LineIndex.html) for the
byte↔(line, column) and byte↔UTF-16 conversions LSP clients need.

All offsets are **byte** offsets into a file’s UTF-8 source. No logic beyond the
conversions lives here. The crate is `wasm32`-safe (no `std::fs`, clocks, threads).

These POD result structs are the analyzer’s **public wire contract** (consumed via
[ gdscript_ide](https://docs.rs/gdscript-ide)), so every public item is documented and

`#![deny(missing_docs)]` keeps it that way.## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [semantic_](https://docs.rs/semantic_token_modifier/index.html)- token_ - modifier
- Bit flags for `SemanticToken::modifiers`

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Cancelled](https://docs.rs/struct.Cancelled.html)
- A read query was cancelled by a concurrent change. (Phase 1 never actually cancels, but the type is on the API surface so the Phase 3 salsa swap is source-compatible.)
- [Code](https://docs.rs/struct.CodeAction.html)- Action
- A code action / quick-fix: a titled, optionally-kinded `SourceChange`
- [Completion](https://docs.rs/struct.CompletionItem.html)- Item
- A by-name completion suggestion.
- [Diagnostic](https://docs.rs/struct.Diagnostic.html)
- A diagnostic with a byte range, a stable machine code, a severity, and a message.
- [Document](https://docs.rs/struct.DocumentSymbol.html)- Symbol
- A (possibly nested) symbol in a document’s outline.
- [File](https://docs.rs/struct.FileEdit.html)- Edit
- The edits to apply to one file (non-overlapping; the client sorts and applies them).
- [FileId](https://docs.rs/struct.FileId.html)
- An opaque file handle. The host owns the `FileId`→ text mapping; the library never reads paths.
- [File](https://docs.rs/struct.FilePosition.html)- Position
- A `(file, byte offset)`cursor position.
- [File](https://docs.rs/struct.FileRange.html)- Range
- A (file, range) pair — the atom of cross-file navigation results.
- [Fold](https://docs.rs/struct.FoldRange.html)- Range
- A foldable range.
- [Hover](https://docs.rs/struct.HoverResult.html)- Result
- The result of a hover query: an inferred type / signature label plus engine docs.
- [Inlay](https://docs.rs/struct.InlayHint.html)- Hint
- An inline hint rendered at a byte offset (e.g. the `: int`the engine LSP omits).
- [LineCol](https://docs.rs/struct.LineCol.html)
- A 0-based `(line, column)`position.`col`is a byte offset within the line.
- [Line](https://docs.rs/struct.LineIndex.html)- Index
- Maps byte offsets to/from `(line, column)`and UTF-16 columns.
- [NavTarget](https://docs.rs/struct.NavTarget.html)
- A navigation target (goto-definition / -declaration). Phase 2 only ever points within the same file; cross-file targets arrive in Phase 3.
- [Param](https://docs.rs/struct.ParamInfo.html)- Info
- One parameter within a `SignatureInfo`
- [Reference](https://docs.rs/struct.Reference.html)
- One reference to a symbol (find-references result), including its declaration.
- [Semantic](https://docs.rs/struct.SemanticToken.html)- Token
- A semantic-highlighting token: a source range classified by its contextual/resolved role. Drives
`textDocument/semanticTokens`— intelligence a grammar can’t produce. Modifiers are a bitset of`semantic_token_modifier`
- [Signature](https://docs.rs/struct.SignatureHelp.html)- Help
- The result of a signature-help query at a call site.
- [Signature](https://docs.rs/struct.SignatureInfo.html)- Info
- One signature shown in signature help (GDScript has no overloads, so usually one).
- [Source](https://docs.rs/struct.SourceChange.html)- Change
- A set of edits across one or more files (a cross-file rename, a quick-fix). Phase 3’s rename
spans files, so this is multi-file; a single-file change is just one `FileEdit`
- [Text](https://docs.rs/struct.TextEdit.html)- Edit
- A single text edit: replace `range`with`new_text`.
- [Text](https://docs.rs/struct.TextRange.html)- Range
- A half-open byte range `[start, end)`into a file’s UTF-8 source.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Completion](https://docs.rs/enum.CompletionKind.html)- Kind
- The kind of a completion item.
- [Diagnostic](https://docs.rs/enum.DiagnosticSource.html)- Source
- What analysis layer produced a diagnostic — lets clients group/filter parse vs. type
diagnostics without parsing the `code`.
- [Fold](https://docs.rs/enum.FoldKind.html)- Kind
- What a fold range corresponds to.
- [Inlay](https://docs.rs/enum.InlayHintKind.html)- Hint - Kind
- What an `InlayHint`
- [Reference](https://docs.rs/enum.ReferenceKind.html)- Kind
- Why a token is a reference (rust-analyzer’s `ReferenceCategory`, trimmed).
- [Rename](https://docs.rs/enum.RenameError.html)- Error
- Why a [rename](https://docs.rs/index.html)was refused — the “correct or it refuses” contract. Never a partial edit.
- [Semantic](https://docs.rs/enum.SemanticTokenType.html)- Token - Type
- The semantic role of a `SemanticToken`
- [Severity](https://docs.rs/enum.Severity.html)
- Diagnostic severity.
- [Symbol](https://docs.rs/enum.SymbolKind.html)- Kind
- The kind of a document symbol (a subset of LSP `SymbolKind`, named for GDScript).

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Cancellable](https://docs.rs/type.Cancellable.html)
- The result of a cancellable read query.
- [Markdown](https://docs.rs/type.Markdown.html)
- Documentation rendered as Markdown (engine `BBCode`already converted at codegen time).

# rustc_hash - Rust

## Expand description

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- An implementation of `BuildHasher``FxHasher`
- [FxHasher](https://docs.rs/struct.FxHasher.html)
- A speedy hash algorithm for use within rustc. The hashmap in liballoc by default uses SipHash which isn’t quite as speedy as we want. In the compiler we’re not really worried about DOS attempts, so we use a fast non-cryptographic hash.
- [FxSeeded](https://docs.rs/struct.FxSeededState.html)- State
- `FxSeededState`- `HashMap`types, allowing to use- `FxHasher`

- Type alias for a hash map that uses the Fx hashing algorithm.
- [FxHash](https://docs.rs/type.FxHashMapSeed.html)- MapSeed
- Type alias for a hashmap using the `fx`hash algorithm with`FxSeededState`
- [FxHash](https://docs.rs/type.FxHashSet.html)- Set
- Type alias for a hash set that uses the Fx hashing algorithm.
- [FxHash](https://docs.rs/type.FxHashSetSeed.html)- SetSeed
- Type alias for a hashmap using the `fx`hash algorithm with`FxSeededState`

# gdscript_scene - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/gdscript-scene/0.5.4/target-redirect/gdscript_scene/

## Expand description

`gdscript-scene` — a `.tscn`/`.tres` **text** parser for scene-aware analysis (Phase 4).

Internal layer (not a stable API).Depend on[(the public surface); the items here may change between releases.](https://docs.rs/gdscript-ide)`gdscript-ide`

Godot’s text scene format is INI-like: bracketed section headers (`[node …]`, `[ext_resource …]`,
…) followed by `key = value` property lines. This crate parses that structure — node names,
types, parent paths, attached scripts, `unique_name_in_owner`, and instanced sub-scenes — into a
`SceneModel`**with byte spans**, so the type layer (Phase-4 M1+) can resolve `$Path` /
`%Unique` / `get_node("…")` to a node’s real `Control`/`Node` subclass instead of bare `Node` —
intelligence the Godot editor’s own LSP produces only in-editor and never flows into inference.

**M0 scope:** the pure, wasm-clean [ parse_scene](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_scene.html) (

`&str -> SceneModel`) + the model + byte
spans. It **records**the typing inputs (

`type=`/`script=`/`instance=`); it does **not**resolve a

`Ty` (M1), recurse into instanced sub-scenes, build the project-wide script↔scene index, or
cache via salsa (M1+). See `plans/PHASE-4-M0-PLAYBOOK.md`.**Invariant:** the parser is strictly additive and **never fails** — every binary/malformed/
unknown form degrades to an empty-or-partial model + a [ SceneProblem](https://docs.rs/enum.SceneProblem.html), never a panic or

`Err`.
The floor is always parity with the engine’s `Node`-everywhere baseline.**Portability:** a core crate — wasm32-clean (no `std::fs`, no `Instant`, no threads); `.tscn`
text is injected via the VFS exactly like `.gd`.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [ExtId](https://docs.rs/struct.ExtId.html)
- An `ext_resource`/`sub_resource`id — the opaque, quoted-string key as written (`"1"`,`"1_app"`,`"StyleBoxFlat_x"`). A 3.x bare-int id is normalized to its string form.
- [ExtResource](https://docs.rs/struct.ExtResource.html)
- An `[ext_resource …]`declaration.
- [NodeIdx](https://docs.rs/struct.NodeIdx.html)
- Index of a node into `SceneModel::nodes`
- [Node](https://docs.rs/struct.NodeProp.html)- Prop
- One body property line of a `[node …]`—`key = value`(value skipped). The key may be a bare identifier (an`@export`var or an engine property) or a`group/sub`override path.
- [Scene](https://docs.rs/struct.SceneConnection.html)- Connection
- One `[connection …]`section — a signal wired to a method in the editor. The four spans are the**inner identifier**byte ranges (surrounding quotes excluded), so a rename rewrites exactly the name. A connection has no body.
- [Scene](https://docs.rs/struct.SceneModel.html)- Model
- One parsed `.tscn`/`.tres`. Produced by`crate::parse_scene`**never**an`Err`— every malformed/binary/unknown form degrades to an empty-or-partial model plus a`SceneProblem``PartialEq`/`Eq`so it can be a backdated salsa query result (`Arc<SceneModel>`) in M1.
- [Scene](https://docs.rs/struct.SceneNode.html)- Node
- One `[node …]`section: its header attributes + the two body properties we read.
- [SubResource](https://docs.rs/struct.SubResource.html)
- A `[sub_resource …]`declaration (type only — the value body is skipped).

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Node](https://docs.rs/enum.NodePathResolution.html)- Path - Resolution
- The reason a node path did (not) resolve — for the `INVALID_NODE_PATH`decision (M2).
- [Scene](https://docs.rs/enum.SceneKind.html)- Kind
- Whether the parsed file is a `.tscn`scene (`gd_scene`) or a`.tres`resource (`gd_resource`).
- [Scene](https://docs.rs/enum.SceneProblem.html)- Problem
- A non-fatal problem found during parsing. The parser records these and keeps going — the floor
is always parity with the engine’s `Node`-everywhere baseline.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_scene.html)- scene
- Parse `.tscn`/`.tres`text into a`SceneModel``Err`.
